query: Taking nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 as the starting material, what single intervention could prevent its radiation-induced precipitation while retaining its negligible irradiation hardening and improving its suitability for practical bulk fabrication? Formulate one testable hypothesis for energetic-particle irradiation relevant to fusion service, including comparison with the unmodified alloy at approximately 8 dpa; identify the intervention and mechanism, predict quantitative or directional changes in precipitation, irradiation defects, and hardening, define the applicable irradiation and thermal boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and propose a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a small amount of titanium as a solute addition to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 can prevent radiation-induced precipitation while retaining its negligible irradiation hardening and improving its suitability for practical bulk fabrication under energetic-particle irradiation relevant to fusion service.
generation.mechanism: alloying element effects on defect formation and migration
generation.predicted_outcome: reduced precipitation, retained negligible irradiation hardening, and improved fabricability
generation.boundary: irradiation dose up to 10 dpa, temperature range 400-600°C
generation.uncertainty: lack of specific data on titanium addition effects in this alloy system

falsification_experiment.design: compare irradiated microstructures and hardness of modified and unmodified alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if modified alloy shows increased precipitation or significant hardening at 8 dpa, the hypothesis is falsified
